1  	/**
2  	 * fx in-sandbox runner. This file must remain zero-dependency.
3  	 */
4  	
5  	import { spawnSync } from 'node:child_process';
6  	import { mkdirSync, writeFileSync } from 'node:fs';
7  	import { dirname, join } from 'node:path';
8  	import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url';
9  	
10 	/** @param {{prompt:string}} input */
11 	export function buildFxCliArgs(input) {
12 	  return ['ask', '--yolo', '--json', '--no-color', '--', input.prompt];
13 	}
14 	
15 	/** @param {string} raw */
16 	export function parseFxAskResult(raw) {
17 	  if (!raw || !raw.trim()) return null;
18 	  try {
19 	    const value = JSON.parse(raw.trim());
20 	    if (
21 	      value &&
22 	      typeof value === 'object' &&
23 	      typeof value.output === 'string' &&
24 	      typeof value.exit_code === 'number' &&
25 	      Array.isArray(value.tool_calls)
26 	    ) {
27 	      return value;
28 	    }
29 	  } catch {
30 	    // The caller reports malformed stdout as an agent failure.
31 	  }
32 	  return null;
33 	}
34 	
35 	/** @param {string} raw */
36 	export function isFxSessionDetail(raw) {
37 	  if (!raw || !raw.trim()) return false;
38 	  try {
39 	    const value = JSON.parse(raw.trim());
40 	    return value?.kind === 'session_detail' && Array.isArray(value.history);
41 	  } catch {
42 	    return false;
43 	  }
44 	}
45 	
46 	/** @param {{model?:string}} input */
47 	export function buildFxEnvironment(input) {
48 	  const env = { ...process.env, FX_AUTO_UPGRADE: '0' };
49 	  if (input.model) env.FX_MODEL = input.model;
50 	  else delete env.FX_MODEL;
51 	  return env;
52 	}
53 	
54 	/**
55 	 * @param {import('../plugin/contract.js').AgentRunInput} input
56 	 * @returns {Promise<import('../plugin/contract.js').RunnerResult>}
57 	 */
58 	export async function runAgent(input) {
59 	  const binary = join(input.cwd, '__agent_eval__', 'bin', 'fx');
60 	  const env = buildFxEnvironment(input);
61 	  const res = spawnSync(binary, buildFxCliArgs(input), {
62 	    cwd: input.cwd,
63 	    env,
64 	    encoding: 'utf8',
65 	    maxBuffer: 64 * 1024 * 1024,
66 	  });
67 	
68 	  const stdout = res.stdout || '';
69 	  const stderr = res.stderr || '';
70 	  const output = stdout + stderr;
71 	  const askResult = parseFxAskResult(stdout);
72 	  const processExitCode = res.status == null ? -1 : res.status;
73 	  const agentExitCode = askResult?.exit_code ?? processExitCode;
74 	
75 	  // The supported session projection is richer than fx ask's final summary.
76 	  // Fall back to the ask JSON when a session cannot be read.
77 	  let transcript = askResult ? stdout.trim() : null;
78 	  if (askResult?.session_id) {
79 	    const session = spawnSync(binary, ['session', '--id', askResult.session_id, '--json'], {
80 	      cwd: input.cwd,
81 	      env,
82 	      encoding: 'utf8',
83 	      maxBuffer: 64 * 1024 * 1024,
84 	    });
85 	    if (session.status === 0 && isFxSessionDetail(session.stdout || '')) {
86 	      transcript = session.stdout.trim();
87 	    }
88 	  }
89 	
90 	  const ok = !res.error && processExitCode === 0 && askResult?.exit_code === 0;
91 	  if (!ok) {
92 	    const errorLines = output.trim().split('\n').slice(-5).join('\n');
93 	    const error = askResult?.error || (res.error ? `Failed to run fx: ${res.error.message}` : null);
94 	    return {
95 	      ok: false,
96 	      output,
97 	      transcript,
98 	      observedModel: askResult?.model || null,
99 	      error: error || errorLines || `fx exited with code ${agentExitCode}`,
100	      agentExitCode,
101	    };
102	  }
103	
104	  return {
105	    ok: true,
106	    output,
107	    transcript,
108	    observedModel: askResult.model || null,
109	    error: null,
110	    agentExitCode,
111	  };
112	}
113	
114	const isMain = process.argv[1] && fileURLToPath(import.meta.url) === process.argv[1];
115	
116	if (isMain) {
117	  const input = JSON.parse(process.argv[2]);
118	  let result;
119	  try {
120	    result = await runAgent(input);
121	  } catch (error) {
122	    result = {
123	      ok: false,
124	      output: '',
125	      transcript: null,
126	      observedModel: null,
127	      error: error && error.message ? error.message : String(error),
128	      agentExitCode: -1,
129	    };
130	  }
131	
132	  try {
133	    mkdirSync(dirname(input.resultPath), { recursive: true });
134	    writeFileSync(input.resultPath, JSON.stringify(result));
135	  } catch {
136	    // The marker below remains available when the result file cannot be written.
137	  }
138	
139	  process.stdout.write(
140	    '__AGENT_RESULT__ ' +
141	      JSON.stringify({
142	        ok: result.ok,
143	        observedModel: result.observedModel,
144	        error: result.error,
145	        agentExitCode: result.agentExitCode,
146	      }) +
147	      '\n'
148	  );
149	  process.exit(0);
150	}
</content>

A request matches on its URL, method, headers, and body, so requests that differ in any of these are cached separately. 55 - If there is a match and it is fresh, it will be returned from the cache. 56 - If there is no match or a stale match, Next.js fetches the resource from the remote server and updates the cache with the downloaded resource. Only responses with a `200` HTTP status code are stored. 57 58 > **Good to know**: Caching is opt-in. Set `cache: 'force-cache'` to cache any request, including `POST` and requests that send `authorization` or `cookie` headers. [Draft Mode](/docs/app/guides/draft-mode) bypasses the cache entirely (no read or write). 59 60 ### `options.next.revalidate` 61 62 ```ts 63 fetch(`https://...`, { next: { revalidate: false | 0 | number } }) 64 ``` 65 66 Set the cache lifetime of a resource (in seconds). 67 68 - **`false`** - Cache the resource indefinitely. Semantically equivalent to `revalidate: Infinity`. The HTTP cache may evict older resources over time. 69 - **`0`** - Prevent the resource from being cached. 70 - **`number`** - (in seconds) Specify the resource should have a cache lifetime of at most `n` seconds. 71 72 > **Good to know**: 73 > 74 > - If an individual `fetch()` request sets a `revalidate` number lower than the [default `revalidate`](/docs/app/guides/caching-without-cache-components#route-segment-config-revalidate) of a route, the whole route revalidation interval will be decreased. 75 > - If two fetch requests with the same URL in the same route have different `revalidate` values, the lower value will be used. 76 > - Conflicting options such as `{ revalidate: 3600, cache: 'no-store' }` are not allowed, both will be ignored, and in development mode a warning will be printed to the terminal. 77 78 ### `options.next.tags` 79 80 ```ts 81 fetch(`https://...`, { next: { tags: ['collection'] } }) 82 ``` 83 84 Set the cache tags of a resource. Data can then be revalidated on-demand using [`revalidateTag`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/revalidateTag). The max length for a custom tag is 256 characters and the max tag items is 128. 85 86 ## Memoization 87 88 `fetch` requests using `GET` with the same URL and options are automatically [memoized](/docs/app/glossary#memoization) during a server render pass. If you call the same `fetch` in multiple Server Components, layouts, pages, `generateStaticParams` and `generateViewport`, Next.js executes it only once and shares the result. This is separate from persistent [caching](/docs/app/getting-started/caching): memoization lasts only for a single render pass, while cached responses persist across requests. 89 90 To opt out, pass an [`AbortController`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/AbortController) signal to `fetch`: 91 92 ```js 93 const { signal } = new AbortController() 94 fetch(url, { signal }) 95 ``` 96 97 > **Good to know**: Memoization does not apply in [Route Handlers](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route), since they are not part of the React component tree. 98 99 ## Troubleshooting 100 101 ### Fetch default `auto no cache` and `cache: 'no-store'` not showing fresh data in development 102 103 Next.js caches `fetch` responses in Server Components across Hot Module Replacement (HMR) in local development for faster responses and to reduce costs for billed API calls. 104 105 By default, the [HMR cache](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/serverComponentsHmrCache) applies to all fetch requests, including those with the default `auto no cache` and `cache: 'no-store'` option. This means uncached requests will not show fresh data between HMR refreshes. However, the cache will be cleared on navigation or full-page reloads. 106 107 See the [`serverComponentsHmrCache`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/serverComponentsHmrCache) docs for more information. 108 109 ### Hard refresh and caching in development 110 111 In development mode, if the request includes the `cache-control: no-cache` header, `options.cache`, `options.next.revalidate`, and `options.next.tags` are ignored, and the `fetch` request is served from the source. 112 113 Browsers typically include `cache-control: no-cache` when the cache is disabled in developer tools or during a hard refresh. 114 115 ## Version History 116 117 | Version | Changes | 118 | --------- | ------------------- | 119 | `v13.0.0` | `fetch` introduced. |

events.content:
UserDashboard is now an async server component. It fetches https://api.example.com/user/preferences with cache: 'no-store' so the request is not cached, and it renders theme and language.

The helper follows getStaticData in app/page.tsx: await fetch, return res.json(), and fall back to mock preferences if the API is unavailable. No 'use client' directive, so it stays a server component.
